evidence.observation: 'GC2 adds the opt-in API keyword and CLI flag, packaged guidance and runnable include-backed example. Verify unchanged default output, CLI/API byte parity from an installed wheel' names no command, no Python function, no flag name and no keyword name.

'Compare compact versus ordinary review bytes on the same populated schema fixture.' and 'Document the flag and keyword on existing CLI and Python reference pages.' never say which existing output counts as the 'ordinary review', or which reference pages are meant.

concerns.recommendation: Name the exact CLI subcommand and flag, the API function and keyword, and the existing output used as the ordinary baseline. Capture that default output as a golden file before GC2 lands, so 'unchanged default output' compares against fixed bytes rather than a later rerun.
concerns.title: The CLI command, flag, API function and keyword being extended are never named, so compatibility and parity cannot be falsified

evidence.observation: 'Use a view digest for replay. Check original root bytes and verified transitive include pins before applying evolution because evidence-only changes can preserve the view digest.' The listed view fields include no root SHA-256 or include pins, so the 'original root bytes' cannot be recovered from the view.

The host record lists 'exact view digest' but not the root SHA-256. §6 claims 'Existing evolution preview and apply perform stale-state checks.' Context: src/gnd/evolve/service.py:1715 only compares proposal.expected_model_sha256 against the current root bytes. A host that computes that value after a concurrent round, rather than taking it from the view, passes the check while acting on a stale view, and can then add a duplicate the view never showed.

concerns.recommendation: Have the projection emit, or the API return beside it, the root SHA-256 and the include pins it was rendered from. Require the host to copy that value into expected_model_sha256 and to record it. Add a GC2 test: render the view, add a fact type non-additively elsewhere, then show that a proposal built from the old view is refused as stale.
concerns.title: The view digest is not tied to the root bytes that evolve's stale-state check compares

evidence.observation: 'Issue 295 asks for compact prompt context' yet the only check is 'Compare compact versus ordinary review bytes on the same populated schema fixture.' No comparison outcome is stated as a pass or a fail.

'Measure actual UTF-8 bytes and confine comparisons to the measured fixture.' and 'Record measured sizes and any limitations.' only record a number. A projection larger than the ordinary output would still satisfy this wording.

concerns.recommendation: State a falsifiable criterion on the named fixture, at minimum compact bytes strictly below ordinary bytes, ideally a ratio. Assert it in the GC1 test so that a regression in size fails the build.
concerns.title: Compactness, the issue's headline requirement, has no pass criterion

evidence.observation: 'a first miss followed by successful lookup of an included fact via its role players, and ambiguous deferral.' Neither 'miss' nor 'ambiguous' is defined. The plan excludes search (§7) and gives search to the host (§3), so the example's miss is staged by the script itself.

'A subset miss requires broader investigation or deferral before asserting novelty. The agent may choose a different search route each round.' No check shows that the rule is followed, or that breaking it is detected.

concerns.recommendation: Define ambiguity: for example, two or more fact types with the same ordered role players and no reading match. Make the example take its lookup result from the CLI or API output bytes, not from fixture constants. Assert the negatives: no evolve apply after a deferral, and no novel add after a subset miss that was never broadened.
concerns.title: The retry and deferral evidence is a scripted example with no defined ambiguity and no negative assertions

evidence.observation: 'Version 1 is canonical UTF-8 JSON with a trailing newline.' and 'Use a view digest for replay.' name no encoder. Nor do they say whether the digest covers the trailing newline, or whether it is embedded in the bytes it hashes. Context: the repo already has src/gnd/artifacts.py:174 canonical_json_bytes (with an exact_numbers option), src/gnd/discover/output.py:35 canonical_bytes and src/gnd/export/ilp_amie.py:224 canonical_bytes.

concerns.recommendation: Name the encoder to reuse (artifacts.canonical_json_bytes) and its options. Define the digest as SHA-256 over the exact emitted bytes, newline included, and keep it outside those bytes. Pin the digest of one fixture in a test.
concerns.title: Neither the canonical encoder nor the bytes the view digest covers is defined

evidence.observation: 'Version 1' is asserted, but no schema_version or kind field and no packaged JSON Schema is planned. Context: other outputs ship beside the code as files such as src/gnd/diff.schema.json and src/gnd/discover.schema.json. §5 documents only 'the flag and keyword'.

concerns.recommendation: Emit schema_version and kind in the bytes and ship a packaged schema for the projection. Validate GC1 fixtures against it, so a host can detect a version 2 and refuse it.
concerns.title: The output carries no version field and has no schema file

evidence.observation: 'Preserve meaningful order and use deterministic ordering elsewhere.' lists neither the meaningful orders nor the sort key. 'deterministic bytes' tests only that repeat runs agree; it cannot show that a cosmetic YAML or include reordering leaves the bytes unchanged.

concerns.recommendation: List the meaningful orders (for example role order and reading order) and the sort key used elsewhere (for example the ID by code point). Add permutation tests: reorder fact types and includes in the source and expect identical bytes; swap the role order and expect different bytes.
concerns.title: Ordering rules are not specified, so the digest may change on cosmetic edits

evidence.observation: 'GND supplies a complete read-only inventory of the resolved model.' but only 'registered constraint signatures' are exposed. Nothing says what happens to an unregistered or extension constraint kind, an objectified fact type or a value constraint.
'empty models, unresolved includes' are listed as tests without an expected outcome, such as an exit code or whether partial output is allowed.

concerns.recommendation: Fail closed: refuse to render, with a named exit, any construct the projection cannot represent, and any unresolved include. Alternatively emit an explicit omission marker. Add a test with an unregistered constraint kind.
concerns.title: A 'complete inventory' can silently drop unregistered constructs, and unresolved-include behaviour is not specified

evidence.observation: 'Check the role-specific occurrence before reusing a fact.' and 'Ordered role-player signatures preserve direction.' Context: the guide's shape report already 'lists existing fact types over the same role players' (unattended-growth.md:57-58). A reversed-direction or ring fact type shares the same players.

concerns.recommendation: Define 'role-specific occurrence'. Add a GC2 negative case: a fact type with the same players in reversed roles, and a ring fact type, where the host must not reuse the existing ID.
concerns.title: No test shows that a fact with the same players in reversed roles is not reused

evidence.observation: 'The host records actual prompt scope, full or partial status, exact view digest, queries, inspected IDs, chosen action and source occurrence.' gives no location or format, and GC2 verification never checks the record. Context: the guide already logs rounds through 'gnd evolve summary ... --record D' (unattended-growth.md:60).

concerns.recommendation: Say whether these fields extend the round-summary schema, which is a compatibility change and needs a version bump, or live in a separate host log. Have the GC2 example assert that the fields are present.
concerns.title: The host record's location, format and compatibility are unspecified and nothing verifies it

evidence.observation: 'Expose object IDs and reference modes, fact IDs' and 'Loader checks protect composed ID identity' rely on the loader, but only one 'direct reuse' is checked. Nothing asserts that every emitted ID, including IDs from included files, is the form evolve accepts as an existing ID.

concerns.recommendation: In GC1, assert that every emitted ID resolves through ModelIndex. In GC2, reuse one root element and one included element through evolve preview.
concerns.title: No test checks that emitted IDs round-trip as evolve reuse targets

response.summary: The two-phase scope is sound: one renderer behind both surfaces, evidence excluded, the host left to choose its own search. But several product obligations cannot be implemented or falsified as written. The plan never names the CLI command, API function, flag or keyword it extends, so 'unchanged default output' and the compact-versus-ordinary comparison have no fixed baseline. The view digest is recorded without the root SHA-256 it was rendered from, so the existing compare-and-swap on expected_model_sha256 does not protect a host that works from a stale view. Compactness has no pass criterion. The retry and deferral evidence is a scripted example with no definition of ambiguity and no negative assertions. Smaller risks to schema identity and compatibility: an unnamed canonical encoder, no version field or schema file, an ordering rule that is not specified, silent omission of unregistered constructs, and no test that a reversed-direction fact is not reused.

evidence.observation: "A subset miss requires broader investigation or deferral before asserting novelty." Broader investigation can still leave the host with a subset, so this rule permits a novelty assertion after another partial miss.

concerns.recommendation: State what evidence permits a novelty assertion when prompt scope was partial. Require deferral while coverage remains insufficient, and test repeated partial misses.
concerns.title: Partial searches lack a safe stopping rule

evidence.observation: The contract promises "registered constraint signatures," while GC1 specifies tests for only "guarded and anchored signatures." A projection could omit another registered constraint family and satisfy the stated tests.

concerns.recommendation: Require a fixture or generated check for every registered family, including its referenced IDs and ordered roles, with an explicit failure when a family cannot be represented.
concerns.title: Constraint fidelity is not demonstrated for every registered family

evidence.observation: GC1 says "Compare compact versus ordinary review bytes on the same populated schema fixture," and the controls say "Measure actual UTF-8 bytes and confine comparisons to the measured fixture." Neither sets a passing result; a larger projection would meet both instructions.

concerns.recommendation: Set a byte-size acceptance criterion for the populated fixture and record both measured values against it.
concerns.title: The compactness requirement has no pass criterion

evidence.observation: The plan calls for "stable identifiers" and says to "Verify complete identifiers on fixtures," but presence of IDs does not test whether equivalent composed views retain the same IDs and references.

concerns.recommendation: Compare projected IDs and references across equivalent source representations, including evidence-only edits and reordered fields whose order is not meaningful; include an include-backed fixture.
concerns.title: Identifier presence does not establish stability

response.summary: The plan needs falsifiable checks for compactness, schema fidelity, identifier stability, and novelty decisions after partial searches.

evidence.observation: "Issue 295 asks for compact prompt context, stable identifiers and explicit guidance when a host supplies a subset."
"Compare compact versus ordinary review bytes on the same populated schema fixture."
"Measure actual UTF-8 bytes and confine comparisons to the measured fixture."

concerns.recommendation: Turn the comparison into an assertion: name the fixture and a pass/fail bound (for example compact bytes at most N percent of ordinary review bytes, and a maximum absolute byte count for the projected schema), and record in §4 GC1 that the check fails when the bound is exceeded. Otherwise the headline obligation of issue 295 can never be shown to hold or to fail.
concerns.title: Compactness is measured but never bounded, so the core obligation cannot fail

evidence.observation: The version-1 field list is "Expose object IDs and reference modes, fact IDs, readings and ordered named role players, direct subtype links and registered constraint signatures." with no scope or partial-view marker.
"The host records actual prompt scope, full or partial status, exact view digest, queries, inspected IDs, chosen action and source occurrence."
"explicit guidance when a host supplies a subset" is listed as an issue-295 obligation, but §2 gives it no payload surface.

concerns.recommendation: Add a scope marker plus the set of unresolved includes to the version-1 payload, include both in the digest inputs, and add a GC2 check that a subset render is byte-distinct from the full render of the same model and that the marker names the missing scope. As written, replay from "exact view digest" alone cannot tell a partial context from a full one, which is exactly the condition under which §5's "A subset miss requires broader investigation or deferral before asserting novelty" must fire.
concerns.title: Partial-scope status lives only in the host record, so a subset view is indistinguishable on replay

evidence.observation: "Version 1 is canonical UTF-8 JSON with a trailing newline." and "Preserve meaningful order and use deterministic ordering elsewhere."
The check list names "deterministic bytes" but no ordering key or serialization rule.

concerns.recommendation: Specify the canonicalization concretely: object-key order, separator and whitespace policy, whether non-ASCII is escaped or emitted literally and under which normalization form, number formatting, and the total ordering key (for example code-point order on the composed ID) used wherever order is not meaningful. Add a GC1 check that compares emitted bytes across two fresh interpreter processes with varied hash seeds and against a committed golden file, so "deterministic bytes" is falsifiable rather than a same-run self-comparison.
concerns.title: 'Canonical UTF-8 JSON' and 'deterministic ordering' are undefined, so byte parity and digest replay are unfalsifiable

evidence.observation: "Exclude author evidence, samples, notes and rationale."
"Field allowlists and evidence sentinels check disclosure." is stated as a control, not as a phase verification.

"Verify complete identifiers on fixtures, role order, guarded and anchored signatures, deterministic bytes, included elements, empty models, unresolved includes and evidence-only edits." contains no non-disclosure check, and GC2's list does not add one.

concerns.recommendation: Add an explicit GC1 check that renders a fixture deliberately populated with author evidence, samples, notes and rationale and asserts that no excluded field name, value, or evidence sentinel appears anywhere in the emitted bytes, including inside readings and signatures.
concerns.title: The evidence-exclusion obligation has a control in §6 but no verification in either phase

evidence.observation: "Verify unchanged default output, CLI/API byte parity from an installed wheel, direct reuse, a first miss followed by successful lookup of an included fact via its role players, and ambiguous deferral."
Closure runs "repository-prescribed checks, component and layer checks, wheel installation, CLI/API parity, and the packaged host example" but names no pre-change baseline artifact.

concerns.recommendation: Name the compatibility baseline: commit golden bytes for the default (non-opt-in) review rendering captured before the GC2 change, or require the check to diff against the previously released wheel, and state in §4 GC2 that the default path must be byte-identical to that baseline. Without a named baseline, "unchanged default output" cannot be demonstrated to a reviewer.
concerns.title: 'Unchanged default output' names no baseline, so the compatibility claim is unverifiable

evidence.observation: "Use a view digest for replay." with no algorithm or input set, followed by "Check original root bytes and verified transitive include pins before applying evolution because evidence-only changes can preserve the view digest."
"exact view digest" is a required host-record field, so consumers depend on its stability.

concerns.recommendation: State the digest algorithm, whether it covers the canonical payload bytes or a structured field subset, and whether the version marker and unresolved-include set are digest inputs. Add a GC1 check that the same model yields an identical digest across processes, and that an evidence-only edit preserves the digest while a mutated root byte or an unverified transitive include pin is rejected before evolution is applied.
concerns.title: The view digest has no defined algorithm or input set, weakening the replay and stale-state guarantees

evidence.observation: "Expose object IDs and reference modes, fact IDs, readings and ordered named role players"
"Loader checks protect composed ID identity." protects the loader, not the renderer's emitted form.
"Verify complete identifiers on fixtures" leaves "complete" undefined, while §5 requires the host to record "inspected IDs".

concerns.recommendation: State in §2 that emitted IDs are exactly the composed loader IDs with no renderer-local aliasing, abbreviation, or re-encoding, and add a GC1 check that every emitted object and fact ID resolves through ModelIndex on the composed model. The compactness pressure noted separately makes ID shortening a likely future temptation, and §5's retry loop depends on those IDs staying resolvable.
concerns.title: Nothing forbids renderer-local ID aliasing, which would break agent-directed lookup by inspected ID

evidence.observation: "Version 1 is canonical UTF-8 JSON with a trailing newline." fixes a version in prose but the enumerated payload contents include no version field.
"Existing additive evolution gates govern writes." implies the underlying model can gain fields after version 1 ships.
"release publication are outside these two phases", so version 1 reaches hosts without a publication gate that could carry the version out-of-band.

concerns.recommendation: Require a version marker inside the payload, define consumer behaviour on an unrecognised version, and state that the projection tolerates model fields added by later additive evolution without changing version 1 semantics. Otherwise digest comparisons across versions are ambiguous and any future field addition is silently breaking for a host that stored only the digest.
concerns.title: The payload carries no version marker, so consumers cannot detect projection version or reject an incompatible one

evidence.observation: "ordered named role players" says nothing about unnamed roles or two roles of the same type on one fact.
"Ordered role-player signatures preserve direction." is the stated control for direction.
"Check the role-specific occurrence before reusing a fact." presumes occurrences are distinguishable per role.

concerns.recommendation: Define the ordering key and the disambiguation rule for anonymous roles, repeated roles of the same type, and multi-role facts, and add a GC1 fixture containing a duplicate-role fact that asserts the emitted signature preserves which player filled which occurrence. Ambiguity here is a direct schema-identity risk because the signature is what an agent reuses a fact on.
concerns.title: Role-player ordering is undefined for anonymous and repeated roles, risking direction and occurrence errors

evidence.observation: "The host owns passage selection, search strategy and prompt budgeting."
"Search indexes, ranking algorithms, hosted inference, new databases, empirical recall claims and release publication are outside these two phases."
"A subset miss requires broader investigation or deferral before asserting novelty." assumes the agent can tell that its view was cut down.

concerns.recommendation: State in §2 or §3 that the renderer never truncates and always emits a complete projection, that any reduction is a host decision which must flip the partial marker described above, and that the CLI/API surface reports the payload byte size so a host can budget before prompting. Silent truncation by either side is the failure mode that turns a subset miss into a false novelty assertion.
concerns.title: No statement of renderer behaviour when the projection exceeds a host prompt budget

evidence.observation: "The earlier five-phase proposal is archived in historical-fable-draft.md." gives a bare filename with no repository-relative path.
"Record current decisions and exact artifacts."

concerns.recommendation: Give the repository-relative path for historical-fable-draft.md so the archived rationale and the passage-selection experiments cited in §1 are locatable from the plan, matching §8's "exact artifacts" requirement.
concerns.title: The archived prior proposal is cited by bare filename with no path

evidence.observation: "The implementation predates formal review."
"Phase records must link implementation, independent opinions and regression results." requires links but no per-obligation comparison of built behaviour to §2.

concerns.recommendation: Add a closure obligation that each phase record states, for every §2 contract item, whether the as-built renderer matches the plan text, and lists any divergence together with the owner decision that accepted it. Since the code exists already, this is the only place a plan-versus-build drift can be surfaced.
concerns.title: Closure links implementation records but never reconciles as-built behaviour against the §2 contract

response.summary: The two-phase plan is coherent and correctly keeps search strategy and budgeting with the host, but five product obligations cannot be falsified from the stated evidence: compactness is only measured, never bounded; the canonical byte form and the total ordering rule are undefined; partial-scope status is assigned to the host record rather than the payload, so digest replay cannot distinguish full from subset context; the author-evidence exclusion has a control in section 6 but no named check in section 4; and 'unchanged default output' names no baseline artifact. Five further risks touch schema identity, view-digest definition, payload versioning, role-player ordering for unnamed or duplicate roles, and truncation behaviour. Two completeness items concern an unlocatable archived reference and as-built reconciliation.

evidence.observation: Section 1 states: "Issue 295 asks for compact prompt context, stable identifiers and explicit guidance when a host supplies a subset." Section 2 defines the schema but omits this guidance: "Version 1 is canonical UTF-8 JSON with a trailing newline. Expose object IDs and reference modes, fact IDs, readings and ordered named role players, direct subtype links and registered constraint signatures. Preserve meaningful order and use deterministic ordering elsewhere. Exclude author evidence, samples, notes and rationale. Use a view digest for replay."

concerns.recommendation: Update Section 2 (Product contract) to explicitly include a subset or partial status indicator within the JSON projection, ensuring the agent receives explicit guidance to inform its retry or deferral logic.
concerns.title: Product contract lacks explicit subset guidance in schema

response.summary: The product contract lacks schema fields to fulfill the explicit subset guidance requirement, blocking agent-directed retry.

evidence.observation: GC1 verification is 'Compare compact versus ordinary review bytes on the same populated schema fixture' and closure says 'Record measured sizes and any limitations.' Neither names a threshold, ratio, or budget that the comparison must satisfy; section 6 even says 'Measure actual UTF-8 bytes and confine comparisons to the measured fixture.' Section 1 states issue 295 'asks for compact prompt context' and 'establish[s] no product-level accuracy or cost improvement,' so compactness is the primary claimed benefit, yet no stated evidence can ever fail it.

concerns.recommendation: Add an explicit, measurable acceptance criterion for compactness (e.g., a maximum compact-to-ordinary byte ratio on named fixtures, or a byte budget per model scale) to GC1 or section 9, so the comparison can falsify the plan.
concerns.title: Compactness has no falsifiable acceptance threshold

evidence.observation: The product contract says 'Exclude author evidence, samples, notes and rationale.' Section 6 lists 'Field allowlists and evidence sentinels check disclosure' as a control, but the GC1 verification list ('Verify complete identifiers on fixtures, role order, guarded and anchored signatures, deterministic bytes, included elements, empty models, unresolved includes and evidence-only edits') and the GC2 list contain no test asserting that excluded content is absent from output; 'included elements' covers only presence.

concerns.recommendation: Add a GC1 verification asserting that author evidence, samples, notes and rationale are absent from the serialized projection (a sentinel/negative test), matching the allowlist and evidence-sentinel controls in section 6.
concerns.title: Exclusion of evidence, samples, notes and rationale has no falsifying test

response.summary: The plan is coherent on schema identity (loader checks, deterministic bytes, guarded/anchored signatures), compatibility (unchanged default output, CLI/API byte parity from an installed wheel), and agent-directed retry (miss-then-lookup, ambiguous deferral, recorded view digest). However, the central product obligation — compactness — has no falsifiable acceptance criterion anywhere in the plan: GC1 only compares bytes and section 9 only records measured sizes, so the compact-versus-ordinary comparison can never fail. Additionally, the exclusion of author evidence, samples, notes and rationale is stated as a product contract but has no corresponding negative-disclosure test in either phase's verification list.

evidence.observation: "Issue 295 asks for compact prompt context, stable identifiers and explicit guidance when a host supplies a subset."

The contract exposes "object IDs and reference modes, fact IDs, readings and ordered named role players, direct subtype links and registered constraint signatures" -- no completeness or subset marker is among the exposed fields.

"The host records actual prompt scope, full or partial status, exact view digest, queries, inspected IDs, chosen action and source occurrence." Full/partial status is a host-side record; the plan never states it is communicated to the consuming agent, yet Section 5 also demands "A subset miss requires broader investigation or deferral before asserting novelty."

"a first miss followed by successful lookup of an included fact via its role players, and ambiguous deferral" exercises retry after a miss, but no listed check asserts the agent was told the supplied context was partial.

concerns.recommendation: State where the subset indicator lives for whoever reads the prompt (a field in the versioned view, or a preamble mandated by the packaged host protocol guide), and add a GC2 acceptance criterion that an include-backed partial view is explicitly marked as not full.
concerns.title: Subset guidance requirement has no agent-visible artifact feature or falsifiable check

evidence.observation: "Version 1 is canonical UTF-8 JSON with a trailing newline." ... "Use a view digest for replay." The canonicalization rules (key ordering, separators, unicode escaping, number formatting) and whether the version marker is embedded in the artifact are unstated.

The only byte-stability evidence is "deterministic bytes" and "CLI/API byte parity from an installed wheel" -- both run in one environment on one wheel, so cross-platform or cross-version canonicalization drift that changes replay digests would pass.

concerns.recommendation: Pin the canonicalization profile by name or documented house rules, state whether "Version 1" travels inside the artifact, and derive the view digest from exactly those rules so replay identity is well defined.
concerns.title: Canonical JSON form and version marker are named but not pinned, weakening digest replay

evidence.observation: "Exclude author evidence, samples, notes and rationale."
"Field allowlists and evidence sentinels check disclosure." -- a control, but assigned to no phase.

The GC1 verify list covers "complete identifiers on fixtures, role order, guarded and anchored signatures, deterministic bytes, included elements, empty models, unresolved includes and evidence-only edits" -- no check that excluded fields are absent from compact output.

concerns.recommendation: Schedule the sentinel test inside GC1: inject marker strings into author evidence, samples, notes and rationale on the fixture and assert they do not appear in the compact bytes.
concerns.title: Disclosure-exclusion control is described but not scheduled as a falsifiable check

evidence.observation: "Use a view digest for replay. Check original root bytes and verified transitive include pins before applying evolution because evidence-only changes can preserve the view digest."
"evidence-only edits" appears as a verify topic with no expected outcome (digest unchanged AND evolution still gated, or something else).

"Existing evolution preview and apply perform stale-state checks." -- pin verification is attributed to existing machinery even though the compact view digest is a new surface; whether those existing checks already verify "verified transitive include pins" is not evidenced.

concerns.recommendation: Spell out the fixture outcome (view digest identical, evolution still blocked on root-byte or transitive-pin mismatch) and confirm or extend the existing stale-state checks so verified transitive include pins are covered on the compact path.
concerns.title: Evidence-only-edit and include-pin evolution gating has no stated expected outcome

evidence.observation: "Issue 295 asks for compact prompt context, stable identifiers and explicit guidance when a host supplies a subset."
"Loader checks protect composed ID identity." -- asserted, with no cited test.
"Verify complete identifiers on fixtures" checks completeness of identifiers, not their stability across edits, even though composed IDs can change when their inputs change.

concerns.recommendation: Add a GC1 fixture asserting identifiers are unchanged under an evidence-only edit and change only in the documented way under a targeted rename, so "stable identifiers" has stated falsifiable evidence.
concerns.title: Stable-identifiers obligation rests on an asserted loader control with no stability test

evidence.observation: "Compare compact versus ordinary review bytes on the same populated schema fixture." No expected relation or bound is stated, so the comparison cannot fail.
"Measure actual UTF-8 bytes and confine comparisons to the measured fixture." -- measurement is confined but no direction or threshold is declared for the milestone's namesake property.

concerns.recommendation: State the expected relation on the fixture (compact strictly fewer bytes than ordinary review output, or a recorded ratio threshold), or explicitly record compactness as measured-but-unclaimed alongside the Section 9 limitations.
concerns.title: Compactness byte comparison lacks an acceptance criterion

evidence.observation: "Preserve meaningful order and use deterministic ordering elsewhere." Which sequences besides role players are "meaningful", and what sort key orders everything else, are unstated.
"role order" and "deterministic bytes" are verified, but a silent re-sort of a meaningful sequence or insertion-order leakage would still pass single-machine determinism tests.

concerns.recommendation: Enumerate the meaningfully ordered sequences and the deterministic sort key per element kind in the versioned format description, so ordering is a format rule rather than an implementation accident.
concerns.title: Meaningful-versus-deterministic ordering rules are not enumerated

response.summary: Digest matched. The two-phase plan states implementable obligations with mostly concrete falsification (deterministic bytes, installed-wheel CLI/API parity, unchanged default output, retry-after-miss via role players, ambiguous deferral), but the issue-295 subset-guidance requirement has no agent-visible artifact feature or acceptance criterion, and several named controls (canonical JSON profile, disclosure sentinels, evidence-only evolution gating, composed-ID stability) lack scheduled, outcome-bearing checks.

criteria: Can each product obligation be implemented and falsified with the stated evidence?
Identify concrete risks to schema identity, compactness, compatibility or agent-directed retry and cite a plan location.
rubric.name: Issue 295 milestone review
